title: The reaction test
one: A new form with twelve pictures, two timers and a ten-second score.

screens.title: Choose your own look and save your pictures
screens.goal: This part is where YOUR test becomes different from MINE. You choose the look, then save your pictures where the program can find them.

open.what: Every reaction test works the same way underneath. The shape, the pictures and the timing are YOUR choices.
open.does: When it works, your four choices are written down. Your pictures sit in the Images folder.

screens.title: Choose how YOUR reaction test will look
screens.done: you have read all four cards
screens.goal: The idea of the test stays the same, but the look of mine is my own choice.

blocks.p: In MY example, the red and yellow flag scores a point. The red flag and the black and white flag lose one.

screens.done: your four choices are written down

blocks.p: Decide four things: your shape, your pictures, which boxes swap, and your time and speed.

stages.title: The reaction test form: its pictures and buttons

screens.title: Make the reaction test form
screens.goal: This part adds frmTest and puts everything on it: twelve picture boxes, a score panel and two timers. A timer is a clock that ticks in code.

open.what: Nothing works yet. This part only lays the form out, the way you laid out the quiz form.
open.does: When it works, frmTest has twelve picture boxes, a score panel and two timers under it.

screens.title: Add the reaction test form
screens.done: frmTest is in Solution Explorer with its two labels on it
screens.goal: A new form called frmTest is in Solution Explorer, with a title label and an instructions label.

blocks.p: The reaction test gets a form of its own, added the way you added the quiz.

steps.see: A box opens with Form picked in its list.

steps.do: In the Name box at the bottom, type frmTest.cs. Click Add.

steps.do: Drag two labels onto the top of the form. Name them lblSafeToSwimSprint and lblInstructions.
steps.see: Two labels sit at the top of frmTest.

screens.title: Add twelve picture boxes
screens.done: twelve picture boxes named pbx1 to pbx12 sit on frmTest

blocks.p: Make one picture box with the right settings, then make eleven more the same.

steps.do: Drag one PictureBox from the Toolbox onto the form.
steps.see: A square picture box sits on the form.

steps.do: In Properties, set SizeMode to StretchImage. Set its Size, for example 100, 100.
steps.see: The picture box is the size you want.

steps.do: Right-click the picture box and click Copy. Right-click the form and click Paste.
steps.see: A second picture box appears. Do this until there are twelve.

steps.do: Drag them into YOUR shape. Name them pbx1 to pbx12, left to right, row by row.
steps.see: Twelve picture boxes, pbx1 at the top left.

screens.goal: The score panel holds the Start button, the score, the time left, the pupil's name and the ? button.

blocks.p: Drag a panel onto the form, then drag each control in the table into it.

controls.done: The last five sit inside pnlReactionTestStats. The ? button gets its code in chapter 13.

blocks.yours: lblTime shows 10 because MY test lasts 10 seconds. Type the number of seconds YOU chose.

screens.title: Meet the two timers and the new words
screens.done: you have read what the two timers do and seen the word list
screens.goal: I know what tmrSwap and tmrCountdown are for before I add them.

blocks.p: The test needs two clocks: one swaps the pictures and the other counts the seconds down.
Below are the new words in this chapter, each with the screen it first appears on.

words: A control you cannot see that ticks on its own.
The gap between ticks. 1000 means one second.
A list that holds picture boxes.
The picture box that was clicked.
The path of the picture it shows.
Take this path exactly as typed.
Do this once for each thing in the list.
blocks.intro: Eleven new things in this chapter. Click any marked word to see what it means.

screens.title: Add two timers
screens.done: tmrSwap and tmrCountdown sit under the form with Interval 1000
screens.goal: Two timers called tmrSwap and tmrCountdown sit in the grey strip under the form, each with Interval 1000.

blocks.p: Timers live in the grey strip under the form, not on it.

steps.do: In the Toolbox, find [[Timer|0]]. Drag it onto the form, twice.
steps.see: Two timers sit in a grey strip under the form, not on it.

steps.do: Name them tmrSwap and tmrCountdown. Set the [[Interval|1]] of each one to 1000.
steps.see: Each timer ticks once every second. Leave Enabled unticked. The code starts them.

blocks.yours: 1000 is one second. If YOUR pictures swap every 0.7 seconds, type 700 for tmrSwap.

screens.title: Type the code that runs as the test form opens
screens.goal: This part types two lines at the top of frmTest's code, then its Load event. The Load event is the code that runs when the form opens.

open.what: The Load event shows the pupil's name and puts all twelve picture boxes into one list. Later code uses that list.
open.does: When it works, two new lines sit at the top and frmTest_Load has five new lines.

screens.goal: Two lines at the top of frmTest's code make the countdown start at 10 and make room for a list of picture boxes.

blocks.p: Double-click frmTest in Solution Explorer, then click View along the top and click Code.

code.title: Two lines at the top
code.where: near the top, above the line public frmTest()

private int CountdownValue = 10;
private List<PictureBox> pictureboxes;

A whole number that starts at 10. The countdown takes one off each second.
Room for a list

screens.title: Make one piece of code for every picture click
screens.goal: This part makes PictureBox_Click. It runs when any of the twelve boxes is clicked.

open.what: Normally each button gets its own click code. Here one piece of code serves all twelve boxes.
open.does: When it works, PictureBox_Click has 17 lines. A click scores a point or loses one, then hides the picture.

screens.title: Type the first line of the click code yourself
screens.done: lines 1 to 5 are typed and the code has no red squiggles
screens.goal: One piece of code, PictureBox_Click, runs for any of the twelve boxes, and it finds out which box was clicked.

blocks.p: Until now a double-click wrote the first line for you, but this one you type yourself.
[[sender as PictureBox|3]] is the box that was clicked. [[!=|4]] means is not.

code.title: The click code: code 1 of 2
code.where: under the last curly bracket of frmTest_Load
partLines: The first line
Type the whole line and the curly bracket yourself. No double-click makes this one.
Which box was clicked?
sender is the box that was clicked. as PictureBox treats it as a picture box.
Only if a box was clicked
null means nothing. The lines below run only when there is a box.

blocks.watch: Type PictureBox_Click exactly. Screen 6-3 joins all twelve boxes to this name.

screens.title: Score the click and hide the picture
screens.done: lines 6 to 17 are typed and the code has no red squiggles
screens.goal: A click on the winning picture adds one to the score, any other picture takes one off, and the picture hides.

blocks.p: A path is where a picture file lives, folder and file name together.
[[ImageLocation|5]] is the path of the picture a box shows.
The [[@ sign|6]] keeps the path exactly as typed.

code.title: The click code: code 2 of 2
partLines: Win or lose a point
If the box shows the winning picture, add one. Otherwise take one off.
Show the score, hide the box
The score turns into words for lblScore. The clicked box hides.
Close both curly brackets
The first closes the if. The last ends the click code.
code.yours: MY winning picture is RedAndYellowFlag.jpeg. Type YOUR winning picture's file name, exactly as you saved it.
